title: The western tip of the Mojave
text: The Antelope Valley covers about 2,200 square miles, mostly in northern Los Angeles County and the southeast corner of Kern County. It is bounded by the Garlock and San Andreas fault systems. Joshua trees, California scrub oak, creosote, and wildflowers, notably the California poppy, grow there. People in the valley depend mainly on pumping groundwater from the valley's aquifers and on importing water from the California Aqueduct.
